turns.doctor_question: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what brought you in to see me?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, thanks. Um, well, I'm here because I'm having a lot of trouble at work. I work at a meat processing plant, and I just keep starting my tasks—like the sanitation steps, the batch logs, or the end-of-line paperwork—and I somehow always leave out the last parts. 

It's becoming a huge problem because I know my job completely depends on finishing those forms and steps correctly, but I just... don't follow through to the end of them.

symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient explicitly states they fail to finish their workplace duties, such as sanitation steps and paperwork, and do not follow through to the end of them.

turns.doctor_question: Has this tendency to leave tasks unfinished been something you've noticed since you were a child, or is this a new pattern that started more recently?
turns.patient_response:
It's definitely not a new thing. It's been happening since I was a kid. 

My mom actually still has some of my old elementary school report cards, like from around fourth grade, and they say pretty much the same thing. The teachers would write that I was bright, but that I needed constant reminders to finish my classwork and actually turn my homework in. I remember I would understand the lessons perfectly fine, but I would just... miss whole chunks of the instructions unless the teacher stayed right close to me to keep me on track.
